extracted.intended_audience: Users/developers of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (computational algebraists/programmers using SINGULAR libraries)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR library procedures (resources.lib, ring.lib, tasks.lib) describing usage, return values, notes, cautions and examples for each procedure. Intended to guide correct invocation and behavior expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: setcores
rubrics_metrics.description: setcores(n), n int — The number of available processor cores is set to n and n is returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The number of available processor cores must be at least 1. Reducing this number may take some time. This procedure should only be called in the main process of a Singular session and not within any task defined via tasks.lib. Example usage shown (LIB "resources.lib"; setcores(2);). See also addcores, getcores, parallel lib, tasks lib.

rubrics_metrics.name: getcores
rubrics_metrics.description: getcores() — Return: the number of available processor cores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedure should only be called in the main process of a Singular session and not within any task defined via tasks.lib. Example usage: setcores(4); getcores();

rubrics_metrics.name: semaphore
rubrics_metrics.description: semaphore(n), n int — Return: the index of a new semaphore initialized with n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates using system("semaphore", "acquire", sem), system("semaphore", "try_acquire", sem), and system("semaphore", "release", sem) to manage the semaphore. No further notes in this excerpt.

rubrics_metrics.name: changechar
rubrics_metrics.description: changechar(c[,r]); c=list, r=ring — Return: ring R obtained from ring r (default basering) by changing ringlist(r)[1] to c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show changing coefficient characteristic and inspecting resulting ring properties. Useful to alter coefficient characteristic of an existing ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: changeord
rubrics_metrics.description: changeord(neword[,r]); newordstr=list, r=ring/qring — Return: ring R obtained from ring r (default basering) by changing order(r) to neword.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If neword contains composite constructs (e.g., list(list("wp",intvec(2,3)),list(list("dp",1:(n-2))))), the resulting ring gets monomial ordering composed accordingly. Examples show constructing weighted and block orderings via changeord and using on qrings.

rubrics_metrics.name: changevar
rubrics_metrics.description: changevar(vars[,r]); vars=string, r=ring/qring — Return: ring R obtained from ring r (default basering) by changing varstr(r) according to vars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If vars = "t()" and r has n variables, new basering will have variables t(1),...,t(n). If vars = "a,b,c,d" the ring will have variables a,b,c,d. Useful with ringtensor to avoid name conflicts. This procedure uses 'execute' internally.

rubrics_metrics.name: defring
rubrics_metrics.description: defring(ch,n,va,or); ch,va,or=strings, n=integer — Return: ring R with characteristic 'ch', ordering 'or' and n variables with names derived from va.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If va is a single letter and n<=26 then consecutive letters are used; if va includes bracket like "T(" then variables become T(1..n). Useful for defining a ring inside a procedure; uses 'execute'. Examples show specifying characteristics like "0" or "2,A".

rubrics_metrics.name: defrings
rubrics_metrics.description: defrings(n,[p]); n,p integers — Return: ring R with characteristic p [default p=32003], ordering ds and n variables x,y,z,a,b,... if n<=26 (resp. x(1..n) if n>26).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proc uses 'execute'. Examples show defrings(5,0) producing QQ coefficients and defrings(30) producing ZZ/32003 with 30 variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: defringp
rubrics_metrics.description: defringp(n,[p]); n,p=integers — Return: ring R with characteristic p [default p=32003], ordering dp and n variables x,y,z,a,b,... if n<=26 (resp. x(1..n) if n>26).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar to defrings but default ordering dp. Uses 'execute'. Examples show P5=defringp(5,0) and P30=defringp(30).

rubrics_metrics.name: extendring
rubrics_metrics.description: extendring(n,va,o[,iv,i,r]); va,o=strings, n,i=integers, r=ring, iv=intvec or 0 — Return: ring R which extends ring r by adding n new variables in front of (resp. after, if i!=0) the old variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defaults: (i,r)=(0,basering). Characteristic inherited from r. New variable naming rules like defring. Ordering is product ordering of r and ordering derived from 'o' (and iv). If 'o' contains 'c' or 'C' at front/end that affects whole ordering. If local integers are used in ordstr, iv must be provided so extendring can know their values. Behavior with weighted orderings: only one weighted block allowed; iv encodes weight counts and block sizes. Useful for adding deformation parameters. Uses 'execute'; advisable to prefix local names with '@' when used inside procedures. Detailed examples show many ordering transforms and block-size derivations; notes on intvec coverage or excess components handling are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: fetchall
rubrics_metrics.description: fetchall(R[,s]); R=ring/qring, s=string — Create: fetch all objects of ring R (poly/ideal/vector/module/number/matrix) into the basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no 2nd argument names are preserved; if given string like "R" then objects mapped to names with that suffix. Maps 1st,2nd,... variables of R to basering's variables. Caution: fetchall does not work for locally defined names and does not work if R contains a map. Example shows usage between rings R and S. See also imapall.

rubrics_metrics.name: imapall
rubrics_metrics.description: imapall(R[,s]); R=ring/qring, s=string — Create: map all objects of ring R into the basering by applying imap to all objects of R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no 2nd argument names are preserved; mapping maps R variables to basering variables with the same name, other variables mapped to 0. Caution: imapall does not work for locally defined names and does not work if R contains a map. Example demonstrates mapping with some variables mapped to 0. See also fetchall.

rubrics_metrics.name: mapall
rubrics_metrics.description: mapall(R,i[,s]); R=ring/qring, i=ideal of basering, s=string — Create: map all objects of ring R into the basering by mapping the j-th variable of R to the j-th generator of ideal i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent to defining map psi=R,i and applying psi to all objects of R. Maps from R to some ring S are composed with psi creating maps from basering to S. mapall may be combined with copyring to change variables for all objects. 3rd argument s used to avoid name conflicts; empty string allowed. Caution: mapall does not work for locally defined names. Examples show different mapping scenarios (constants, expressions, identity maps).

rubrics_metrics.name: ord_test
rubrics_metrics.description: ord_test(r); r ring/qring — Return: int 1 (resp. -1, resp. 0) if ordering of r is global (resp. local, resp. mixed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ord_test(R) for dp ordering returns 1; for ls local ordering returns -1; for mixed rings returns 0. See also Section 5.1.2 [attrib].

rubrics_metrics.name: ringtensor
rubrics_metrics.description: ringtensor(r1,r2,...); r1,r2,...=rings — Return: ring R whose variables are the variables from all rings r1,r2,... and whose monomial ordering is the block (product) ordering of the respective monomial orderings; R is the tensor product of the rings r1,r2,...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characteristic of result will be p if one ring has characteristic p. Variable names in input rings must differ. Works also for quotient rings ri if characteristic of ri is compatible (i.e., if imap from ri to result is implemented). Examples show combining rings and qrings, creating QRings from ideals and combining them into ringtensor. See also ring operations section.

rubrics_metrics.name: ringweights
rubrics_metrics.description: ringweights(P); P=name of an existing ring — Return: intvec consisting of the weights of the variables of P, as they appear when typing P;.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when enlarging P but keeping weights of old variables. Example: ringweights(r0) -> 1,1,1; ring r1 weights returned and used to construct new ring with specific weights and ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: preimageLoc
rubrics_metrics.description: preimageLoc ( ring name, map name, ideal name ); all input parameters of type string — Return: ideal. Purpose: compute the preimage of an ideal under a given map for non-global orderings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2nd argument must be the name of a map from the basering to the given ring (or the name of an ideal defining such a map), and the ideal has to be an ideal in the given ring. Example demonstrates calling preimageLoc("R","psi","null"). See also preimage entry in main doc.

rubrics_metrics.name: rootofUnity
rubrics_metrics.description: rootofUnity(n); n an integer — Return: number. Purpose: compute the minimal polynomial for the n-th primitive root of unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: works only in field extensions by one element. Examples: rootofUnity(6) -> (q2-q+1); rootofUnity(7) -> cyclotomic polynomial; minpoly can be set to rootofUnity(8) etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: optionIsSet
rubrics_metrics.description: optionIsSet(optionName) — Parameters: optionName: a name as string of an option of interest. Return: true if option is active, false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: optionIsSet("warn") returns 0 initially; after option("warn") returns 1; after option("nowarn") returns 0 again. Useful to check runtime options.

rubrics_metrics.name: hasNumericCoeffs
rubrics_metrics.description: hasNumericCoeffs(rng) — Return: 1 if rng has inexact coefficients, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: integer coefficient ring -> 0; complex coefficient ring -> 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: hasCommutativeVars
rubrics_metrics.description: hasCommutativeVars(rng) — Return: 1 if rng is a commutative polynomial ring, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ring r=0,(x,y,z),dp; hasCommutativeVars(r) -> 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: hasGlobalOrdering
rubrics_metrics.description: hasGlobalOrdering(rng) — Return: 1 if rng has a global monomial ordering, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: integer,x,dp -> 1; 0,x,ds -> 0. Useful to detect ordering type programmatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: hasMixedOrdering
rubrics_metrics.description: hasMixedOrdering() — Return: 1 if ordering of basering is mixed, 0 else.

rubrics_metrics.name: hasAlgExtensionCoefficient
rubrics_metrics.description: hasAlgExtensionCoefficient(rng) — Return: 1 if coefficients are an algebraic extension, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: integer,x,dp -> 0; (0,a),x,dp with minpoly=a2-1 -> 1; (49,a),x,dp -> 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: hasTransExtensionCoefficient
rubrics_metrics.description: hasTransExtensionCoefficient(rng) — Return: 1 if the coefficients are rational functions, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: integer,x,dp -> 0; (0,a),x,dp -> 1; (49,a),x,dp -> 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: isQuotientRing
rubrics_metrics.description: isQuotientRing(rng) — Return: 1 if rng is a quotient ring, 0 otherwise. Purpose: check if typeof a rng "qring".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ring rng = 0,x,dp -> 0; qring q = ideal(x) constructs rng/ideal(x) -> isQuotientRing(q) returns 1. Suggestion: use in ASSUME checks when methods don't support quotient rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: isSubModule
rubrics_metrics.description: isSubModule(I,J) — Return: 1 if module(I) is in module(J), 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: I1=x2, I2=x3; isSubModule(I1,I2) -> 0; isSubModule(I2,I1) -> 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: changeordTo
rubrics_metrics.description: changeordTo(ring, string s) — Return: a ring with the ordering changed to the (simple) ordering s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: changeordTo(r,"dp") returns a new ring with dp ordering. Useful for simple ordering changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: addvarsTo
rubrics_metrics.description: addvarsTo(ring,list of strings,int) — int may be: 0:ordering dp; 1:ordering dp,dp; 2:ordering.ordering,dp — Return: a ring with the additional variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show addvarsTo(r,list("a","b"),0/1/2) producing rings with different block/order placements. The integer parameter controls how new variable blocks are added relative to existing ordering blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: addNvarsTo
rubrics_metrics.description: addNvarsTo(ring,int N, string name, int b); b may be: 0:ordering dp; 1:ordering dp,dp; 2:ordering.ordering,dp — Return: a ring with N additional variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: addNvarsTo(r,2,"@",0/1/2) producing variables named @(1),@(2) with different ordering placements. Shows how block/order assignments change depending on b.

rubrics_metrics.name: tasks.lib overview
rubrics_metrics.description: tasks.lib — A parallel framework based on tasks. Introduces a new Singular type 'task' representing a command string applied to a list of arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tasks can be computed in parallel and started recursively (from within other tasks). tasks.lib respects computational resource limits defined in resources.lib: all tasks in same Singular session will not use more computational resources than provided via resources.lib, even if started recursively. parallel.lib provides higher-level parallel skeletons built on tasks.lib. Procedures documented include createTask, killTask, copyTask, compareTasks, printTask, startTasks, stopTask, waitTasks, waitAllTasks, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: createTask
rubrics_metrics.description: createTask(command, arguments), command string, arguments list — Return: a task with the given command and arguments whose state is 'created'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shortcut: 't = command, arguments;' equals createTask. Example shows creating task t = createTask("std", list(I)). See related procedures getCommand, getArguments, getState, copyTask, killTask, startTasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: killTask
rubrics_metrics.description: killTask(t), t task — Return: nothing. Erases internal data structures of t and sets its state to 'uninitialized'. If t was 'started', it is stopped first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: killTask(t) is not the same as 'kill t;' — the latter doesn't erase internal data structures. killTask should be called for any no longer needed task to free memory. Examples demonstrate state transitions and getState returning 'uninitialized' after killTask.

rubrics_metrics.name: copyTask
rubrics_metrics.description: copyTask(t), t task — Return: a copy of task t (a new independent task).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: copyTask creates an independent copy; assignment 'task t1 = t2;' makes t1 point to same object and changes to one affect the other. A task whose state is 'started' cannot be copied. Example demonstrates copying a completed task and accessing its result via getResult on the copy; killTask should then be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: compareTasks
rubrics_metrics.description: compareTasks(t1,t2), t1,t2 tasks — Return: 1 if t1 and t2 coincide; 0 otherwise. Note: The arguments and the results of t1 and t2 are not compared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 't1 == t2' is a shortcut for compareTasks(t1,t2). Example: two separately created tasks with same command/arguments initially compare equal (1), but after starting one they may not. Also shows that tasks with different arguments may still compare equal because arguments/results are not compared.

rubrics_metrics.name: printTask
rubrics_metrics.description: printTask(t), t task — Return: nothing. Prints information about t (state, command, number of arguments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shortcuts: 'print(t);' and just 't;' print task info. Examples show uninitialized/created/started/completed states printed. See getCommand/getArguments/getState/getResult for programmatic access.

rubrics_metrics.name: startTasks
rubrics_metrics.description: startTasks(t1,t2,...), t1,t2,... tasks — Return: nothing. Starts the tasks t1,t2,... and sets their states to 'started'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A task whose state is neither 'created' nor 'stopped' cannot be started. If a task is 'stopped', startTasks restarts computation from beginning. Tasks can be started from within other tasks; a started task should not be accessed from within any task other than the one within which it was started. Start of each task is subject to internal scheduling. Examples show starting multiple tasks and later retrieving results with getResult. See pollTask, waitTasks, stopTask, printTask.

rubrics_metrics.name: stopTask
rubrics_metrics.description: stopTask(t), t task — Return: nothing. Stops t and sets its state to 'stopped'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A task whose state is not 'started' cannot be stopped. Intermediate results are discarded when a task is stopped. killTask() should be called for any no longer needed task. Example shows transition to 'stopped' state.

rubrics_metrics.name: waitTasks
rubrics_metrics.description: waitTasks(T,N[,timeout]), T list of tasks, N int, timeout int — Waits for N tasks to complete and returns an ordered list of indices of those tasks which have been successfully completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets state of returned tasks to 'completed'. Optional timeout in ms (default 0 disables timeout). A task whose state is neither 'started' nor 'completed' cannot be waited for. Returned list may contain more than N entries if some tasks already finished or multiple finished simultaneously, or less than N with timeout/errors. Polling is guaranteed: any task t for which 'pollTask(t);' would return 1 will appear in returned list. Examples demonstrate waiting for both tasks and then calling getResult on each. See pollTask, getResult, getState.

rubrics_metrics.name: waitAllTasks
rubrics_metrics.description: waitAllTasks(t1,t2,...), t1,t2,... tasks — Return: nothing. Waits for all the tasks to complete and sets their state to 'completed'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convenience wrapper to block until all specified tasks finish. Example usage referenced but not expanded in this chunk.
